db_evidence.notes: The event_steps/episodes captions for the 49740-49770s crate-loot window (event_steps:00001301, episodes:30sec:001658, episodes:3min:000276) exist and are reachable by both semantic_search (with generic queries like 'gourd obtained') and run_sql (LIKE %葫芦%, LIKE %gourd%), but the stored caption transcribes the on-screen item name as '缠蛇葫芦' instead of the true '湘妃葫芦' (verified by extracting frames at 49749-49753s, which clearly show the loot notification text '湘妃葫芦'). This is a captioning/OCR error in the memory DB: the correct answer's item name is present in the right time window but under a wrong string that doesn't match any of the four multiple-choice options, so pure text/semantic search over that caption cannot confirm the answer -- only a clip_qa visual read of the actual frame resolves it. Separately, an unrelated vendor listing at 59160s legitimately and correctly contains the string '妙仙葫芦' (option 1's exact name), making it a strong false-positive text match for any search seeded from the four choice names.

root_causes: DB caption/OCR error at the clue window (49740-49770s) mistranscribes the on-screen item name '湘妃葫芦' as '缠蛇葫芦', making the correct evidence textually invisible to keyword/semantic search seeded from the answer choices

1 rollout (1) reached the correct window via SQL but treated the garbled caption as irrelevant since it matched none of the 4 choices, and did not call clip_qa to disambiguate before falling back to the vendor distractor
1 rollout (4) called clip_qa but on the wrong (vendor) window, then ignored its own sub-agent's explicit statement that the item was not obtained there, submitting the vendor's item name anyway

Only the 1 successful rollout (3) both located the crate-loot event_steps row near the clue time via a generic gourd/description SQL search and then used clip_qa specifically to visually re-read the on-screen text, catching the caption/answer-choice mismatch
what_worked: Rollout 3's run_sql query on event_steps with a broad LIKE '%葫芦%'/'%gourd%' filter over a wide time range (48000-61000) surfaced the actual crate-loot event even though its caption text was garbled

Rollout 3 recognized that a garbled/unfamiliar item name near the target scene warranted visual verification rather than being discarded, and used clip_qa on a tight window (49735-49780s) bracketing the clue interval to read the exact on-screen text
Rollout 3's clip_qa correctly OCR'd the true item name '湘妃葫芦' and matched it to the correct multiple-choice option
transferable_lessons: When a candidate item/name found near the target scene does not exactly match any given multiple-choice option, don't discard it as irrelevant -- it may be the correct answer under a caption/OCR error; verify visually with clip_qa before falling back to a distractor that happens to string-match a choice

A caption/topic_facts snippet that verbatim-matches one of the multiple-choice strings is not automatically reliable evidence -- check whether it actually represents the queried event (an 'obtain' action) rather than an unrelated appearance (e.g., a vendor's for-sale listing) of the same item name

When clip_qa's answer explicitly states the target action did NOT occur in the queried window (e.g., 'item not obtained here'), do not submit that item as the answer -- treat it as evidence to rule out that window and search elsewhere

For 'obtain a specific named item' questions, prioritize SQL searches over event_steps/episodes using generic domain terms (e.g., 'gourd', '葫芦', 'obtain', 'loot', 'chest') across the full plausible time range rather than searching per-choice-name, since the choice names may not appear verbatim in captions near the true event but a generic term still will

Always run clip_qa to visually confirm the exact on-screen text for short, precise-answer multiple-choice questions with a narrow clue interval (a few seconds), since DB captions can mis-transcribe visually similar or unfamiliar Chinese item names
